newsitem.title: FRANCE: Number of French workers predicted to keep growing.
newsitem.headline: Number of French workers predicted to keep growing.

text.p: France's working population will keep growing until 2006, after which it will begin tapering off as the baby boom generation begins retiring, two state agencies predicted on Wednesday.

France's current population of 26.6 million working men and women will grow to 28 million in the next decade before shrinking back to 26 million by 2040, the national statistical institute INSEE and the statistical research agency DARES said in a joint study.

The working population has been growing steadily for the past 30 years as the baby-boom generation has reached adulthood, but the decline will take place because the boomers' fertility rate has been falling off, the study found.
The proportion of elderly people in the working population has been steadily shrinking in recent years as individuals retire at an earlier age, it said.
Only nine percent of France's working population were more than 55 years old in 1995, compared to 19 percent in 1968.
